name: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries MGL-8 'Thresher'
description:
A belt-fed automatic grenade launcher designed for vehicle mounting or emplaced defensive positions. The MGL-8 fires standard 40mm grenades from a 32-round belt at a cyclic rate of 300 rounds per minute, creating a sustained barrage that can suppress an area the size of a city block. The weapon weighs 28 kg without ammunition and is not designed for individual carry — it is a crew-served weapon intended for checkpoints, vehicle turrets, and fixed defensive positions.

Zheng-Dao manufactures the Thresher for military customers, but the weapon has appeared in GLMZ's inter-corporate conflicts when escalation moves beyond small arms. During the Tier 4 corridor dispute of 2196, both sides deployed vehicle-mounted Threshers in residential areas, and the resulting collateral damage killed more civilians than combatants. The weapon is effective precisely because it is indiscriminate — 300 grenades per minute turns everything in the target area into debris regardless of its tactical significance.
legality: Military only — prohibited for corporate security deployment (frequently violated)
specifications:
caliber: 40mm standard casings
feed: 32-round disintegrating belt
cyclic rate: 300 rounds per minute
effective range: 75-1,500 meters
weight: 28 kg (weapon only)
mounting: Vehicle turret or tripod emplacement
tactical_use: Area suppression, defensive perimeter enforcement, vehicle convoy protection. Requires a two-person crew for sustained operation — one gunner, one ammunition handler. Effective against light vehicles, personnel in the open, and structures up to reinforced concrete.
cultural_context: The Thresher represents the point where corporate 'security operations' become indistinguishable from warfare. When a Thresher appears, the pretense of proportional response has been abandoned. Journalists covering corporate conflicts use 'Thresher deployment' as shorthand for 'war crime in progress.'
story_hooks: A Thresher has gone missing from a Zheng-Dao armory. The weapon is crew-served, belt-fed, and weighs 28 kg — not something you tuck under your coat. Someone had logistical support to steal it, and logistical support to use it.

A vehicle mounting a Thresher has been spotted on a freight elevator heading toward the upper tiers. Whoever has it is moving it into position for something, and the target area contains 40,000 residents.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist industrial weapon system with a pronounced boxy receiver and prominent belt feed mechanism. The MGL-8 reads as pure mechanical function — no aesthetic concessions, all aggressive angles and utilitarian protrusions. Its silhouette is dominated by the wide ammunition housing and the chunky barrel assembly that dominates the profile.
physical_description.dimensions: 127 cm overall length, 38 cm barrel length, 42 cm width across feed system, 34 cm height at receiver
physical_description.weight_description: Formidable and anchored — 28 kg feels substantial and unyielding in a mounting cradle, designed for crews not individuals. The weight is distributed across a wide footprint, creating a stable but unmovable presence.
physical_description.primary_material: Stamped steel receiver with tungsten-reinforced barrel assembly, aluminum alloy feed housing for weight optimization without sacrificing durability
physical_description.finish: Military matte black oxide coating with industrial wear patterns visible at stress points and contact surfaces. Chrome-lined bore visible through barrel opening. Underlying steel shows through high-friction areas.
physical_description.color_scheme: Flat tactical black primary, with exposed brushed steel and chrome highlights at mechanical interfaces. Faint factory stenciling in gray on the receiver.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized cold-weather grip pads at the dual spade handles, textured to prevent slipping under recoil. Bare steel mounting points where the tripod or gimbal interface accepts the weapon.
distinctive_features: 32-round disintegrating belt visible in open-sided feed mechanism with color-coded ammunition indicators (yellow, red casings)
Hydraulic recoil cylinder running parallel to barrel with pressure relief markings
Dual spade-grip handles positioned low and wide for crew stability during sustained fire
Rapid-traverse mounting gimbal base with degree-marking scales for targeting coordination
Heat vents cut into the receiver around the chamber area with visible scoring from thermal cycling
Heavy-duty feed cover with quick-release lever and ammunition counter dial
Integral muzzle brake assembly with perforated steel shroud showing carbon scoring
Cable routing for electric trigger solenoid visible along left side
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO HEAVY INDUSTRIES stamped in deep relief on both sides of the receiver. Serial plate mounted on right side of frame with manufacturing date (2219) and compliance stamp showing military-only designation. Cautionary symbols in multiple languages etched near firing mechanism.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn with carbon scoring around the muzzle and thermal discoloration on the barrel shroud. Hydraulic fluid residue at seal points. Ammunition belt show handling marks from repeated loading cycles. The weapon operates until failure — maintenance is reactive, not preventive, in most deployments.
